title: ETL vs ELT
interviewAnswer: ETL transforms data before loading it into the target system; ELT loads raw data first and transforms within a powerful warehouse/lakehouse. Choice depends on governance, scale, latency and platform.
why: ETL vs ELT tests whether you understand where transformations happen and how modern data platforms trade control, scalability and governance.
intuition: ETL transforms data before it reaches the analytical destination. ELT loads raw data first and transforms inside the warehouse/lakehouse using its compute.
deepDive: ETL is useful when destination constraints, privacy or standardization require processing before load. ELT preserves raw data and exploits scalable warehouse compute, improving reprocessing/flexibility. Real systems are often hybrid. The important design questions are lineage, schema evolution, idempotency, data quality, cost and whether transformations need to support both batch and near-real-time consumers.
workedExample: An ADF pipeline can extract relational tables, apply SQL transformations and load curated outputs—ETL. A lakehouse workflow might first land raw files, then use Spark/SQL models inside the platform—ELT.
commonMistakes: Ignoring governance and sensitive fields when landing raw data.
Treating ETL/ELT as only a tool choice rather than a data-flow architecture choice.
followUps: Why is ELT common in cloud warehouses?
How do you make pipelines idempotent?
How do you handle schema changes?
production: Track lineage, source timestamps, row counts, checksums and quality expectations at each stage. Backfills and retries should not duplicate or corrupt downstream data.
